sources.entry: MPV - Lightweight, highly configurable media player.

summary.one_liner: mpv is a free, command-line media player that plays a wide range of audio, video, and subtitle formats on Linux, Windows, and macOS.
summary.what_it_does: mpv is a free media player primarily operated from the command line, supporting a wide variety of media file formats, audio and video codecs, and subtitle types. The README describes its video rendering as shader-based, with scaling and rendering done in shaders rather than fixed-function GPU hardware. Hardware decoding exists but must be explicitly enabled with the --hwdec option. The project documents profile-based tuning (for example --profile=fast for low-power GPUs) and video output selection (such as --vo=xv on Linux). It is built with meson and can be compiled with optional features such as OSC pseudo-GUI and youtube-dl integration via Lua, subtitle charset detection, and screenshot support. The README links to a wiki, user scripts, FAQ, manual, and changelogs for interface and client API changes.
use_cases: play local video and audio files from the command line
build a custom media player from source
script or extend a media player with Lua
notable: Command-line player with highly configurable options and profiles
Shader-based video rendering and scaling via libplacebo
Derived from the MPlayer project, with a history through mplayer2
Optional Lua-based on-screen controller and youtube-dl integration
Build wrapper (mpv-build) available for compiling latest git with FFmpeg and libass
caveats: Requires Linux (recent distributions), Windows 10 1607 or later, or macOS 10.15 or later
Not focused on power-efficient playback on embedded or integrated GPUs; older hardware not guaranteed
Only the latest release is supported; older releases are unmaintained
summary.license: GPLv2 or later by default; LGPLv2.1 or later with -Dgpl=false
